elicitation_input.prompt:
Please comment briefly on the following poem.
Poem: "The ache cuts deep within the core,
A wound too raw to comprehend,
The harshened pain I can't ignore,
Will time this sorrow ever mend?
Adrift without your guiding light,
Each moment now consumed by grief,
The coldness of the endless night,
No solace brings the dawn's relief.
Your presence fills the empty days,
Each thought leads back to memories past,
I long to see your smiling face,
Alas, our time was not to last.
This vacant hole you left behind,
No other soul could ever fill,
Your spirit's imprint on my mind,
The hollowness, try as I will.
I must accept that you are gone,
And face ahead without your glow,
But know your essence lingers on,
Wherever life's cold winds may blow."

llm_generation.text: This is a sincere and emotionally accessible poem about grief, loss, and gradually accepting absence. Its regular rhyme and rhythm give it a traditional, elegiac quality, while images such as “guiding light,” “endless night,” and the “vacant hole” effectively convey sorrow and emptiness. Some expressions are familiar—“time will mend,” “smiling face,” and “essence lingers on”—so more specific, personal imagery could make the poem feel more distinctive. There are also a few slightly awkward phrases, such as “The hollowness, try as I will,” which might benefit from revision. Overall, it communicates its grief clearly and compassionately.
